findings.description: storage_encrypted is explicitly set to false, meaning the RDS database data at rest is not encrypted, violating encryption-at-rest requirements for sensitive data.
publicly_accessible is set to true, exposing the RDS instance to the public internet and significantly increasing the attack surface for a database holding credentials and application data.

The database master password is passed via var.password and injected in plaintext into the EC2 user_data script; combined with a static admin username, this risks credential exposure through instance metadata and Terraform state.

The EC2 user_data script embeds the database username and password in plaintext (DB_PASSWORD, DB_USERNAME) which is stored unencrypted in instance metadata, accessible to anyone with access to the instance or the metadata service, and also visible in Terraform state/plan output.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on Resource: '*', giving the EC2 instance role far broader privileges than needed (violates least privilege) and could allow privilege escalation or data exfiltration if the instance is compromised.

The security group egress rule allows all outbound traffic (protocol -1, all ports) to 0.0.0.0/0, which removes network segmentation and could facilitate data exfiltration from a compromised database instance.

backup_retention_period is set to 0, disabling automated backups; while primarily an operational concern, in this context it also removes a recovery path in case of ransomware or data-destruction attacks, a defence-in-depth consideration.
